1: ---
2: name: obscura
3: description: Use Obscura — a Rust headless browser with a Chrome DevTools Protocol server — for fast page fetches, JS execution, scraping, and CDP automation. Drop-in CDP replacement for Chrome with Puppeteer or Playwright. Trigger on requests to "open a page", "fetch a URL with JS", "scrape a site", "render this page", "automate browser via CDP", or any task where Chrome would be too heavy. Also use when the user mentions stealth fingerprinting, tracker blocking, `navigator.webdriver` masking, or evading basic bot detection.
4: ---
5: 
6: # Obscura
7: 
8: Single-developer, open-source Rust headless browser. Boots instantly, ~70 MB binary, ~30 MB RAM at runtime, and serves a Chrome DevTools Protocol port that Puppeteer and Playwright connect to unchanged. **You swap the binary, not the code.**
9: 
10: Repo: https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura
11: 
12: ## Why pick Obscura over Chrome
13: 
14: | | Obscura | Chrome |
15: |---|---|---|
16: | Binary | ~70 MB | ~300 MB |
17: | RAM | ~30 MB | ~200 MB |
18: | Cold start | instant | ~2 s |
19: | Page load (upstream claim) | ~85 ms | varies |
20: 
21: Field measurement on Cloudflare-protected `nairaland.com` (warm fetch): **Obscura ~4.1–4.9 s, returns real HTML body**. Real Chrome over CDP: ~5.1 s warm / 9.3 s cold. `curl`: 0.5–0.9 s but only the CF challenge interstitial.
22: 
23: Obscura is roughly as fast as warm Chrome, ~2× faster cold, parallelizes far better because it doesn't carry Chrome's per-process overhead, and clears Cloudflare's basic JS challenge **without** the stealth feature.
24: 
25: ## Build
26: 
27: ```bash
28: git clone https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura.git
29: cd obscura
30: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/obscura-target cargo build -p obscura-cli --bin obscura --no-default-features
31: ```
32: 
33: Resulting binary: `/tmp/obscura-target/debug/obscura`
34: 
35: `--no-default-features` skips the stealth build. Stealth needs `cmake` locally because it pulls `wreq` / BoringSSL.
36: 
37: ### Stealth build
38: 
39: ```bash
40: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/obscura-target cargo build -p obscura-cli --bin obscura --features stealth
41: ```
42: 
43: What stealth gives you:
44: 
45: - **Per-session randomized fingerprints** — GPU, canvas, audio, battery
46: - **3,520 tracker domains blocked** (built-in blocklist)
47: - **`navigator.webdriver` masked**
48: - **Native functions patched** so common automation detectors can't unmask them via `Function.prototype.toString` inspection
49: - **TLS / HTTP-2 fingerprint** matching real Chromium (defeats most JA3/JA4 + ALPN-ordering bot management)
50: 
51: Use stealth against: Cloudflare Turnstile non-interactive, Akamai BMP, PerimeterX, DataDome.
52: Stealth still won't clear: hard interactive CAPTCHAs (Turnstile interactive, hCaptcha challenge), and fingerprinters using WebGPU/WebAssembly quirks not yet patched.
53: 
54: ## CLI fetch
55: 
56: ```bash
57: /tmp/obscura-target/debug/obscura fetch https://example.com/ --dump text --quiet
58: ```
59: 
60: Useful flags:
61: - `--dump text` — visible text only
62: - `--dump html` — full rendered DOM
63: - `--quiet` — suppress progress logs
64: - `--timeout <ms>` — per-page timeout
65: 
66: ## CDP server (Puppeteer / Playwright)
67: 
68: ```bash
69: /tmp/obscura-target/debug/obscura serve --port 9222
70: ```
71: 
72: **Playwright:**
73: 
74: ```ts
75: import { chromium } from "playwright-core";
76: 
77: const browser = await chromium.connectOverCDP("ws://127.0.0.1:9222");
78: const page = await browser.newContext().then((ctx) => ctx.newPage());
79: await page.goto("https://example.com/");
80: console.log(await page.title());
81: await browser.close();
82: ```
83: 
84: **Puppeteer:**
85: 
86: ```ts
87: import puppeteer from "puppeteer-core";
88: 
89: const browser = await puppeteer.connect({
90:   browserWSEndpoint: "ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser",
91: });
92: const page = await browser.newPage();
93: await page.goto("https://example.com/");
94: console.log(await page.title());
95: await browser.disconnect();
96: ```
97: 
98: ## Scaling profile
99: 
100: - ✅ **High concurrency, low resource:** static + lightly-dynamic pages — hundreds of parallel fetches per box.
101: - ⚠️ **Medium:** JS-rendered SPAs, light bot protection — works but slower than raw HTTP, watch timeouts.
102: - ❌ **Low / unreliable:** aggressive bot defense (Turnstile interactive, Akamai BMP), real auth-walled apps, anything needing pixel-perfect rendering parity with Chrome.
103: 
104: ## Known limits
105: 
106: - Not full Chrome — some browser APIs and CDP methods are incomplete relative to upstream Chromium.
107: - Screenshot capture is not implemented (no layout/rendering engine).
108: - Authenticated pages need cookie or session injection via CDP; Obscura won't run interactive logins.
109: - Hard CAPTCHAs (Turnstile interactive, hCaptcha) require a human or a third-party solver.
110: 
111: ## Safety
112: 
113: Treat Obscura like any external Rust crate: `cargo build` runs dependency build scripts (V8, TLS). Build into a disposable target dir (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/obscura-target`) when evaluating new branches.

5: 
6: # Obscura Browser
7: 
8: ## Overview
9: 
10: Use this skill to help users operate the `obscura` CLI and connect client libraries to its CDP server. Prefer short, executable commands first, then add optional flags or sample code only if they help the user's scenario. For local development, default to `Vite + hostc + Obscura` instead of suggesting localhost access.

12: ## Workflow
13: 
14: 1. Detect whether `obscura` is available locally before giving run commands.
15: 2. If it is missing, explain the shortest install path for the current OS.
16: 3. If the target is local development, do not suggest patching Obscura or using localhost directly. Default to:
17:    - local app on Vite or another dev server
18:    - `hostc` to expose the local port as a public `https://` URL
19:    - Obscura against the public URL
20: 4. Pick the narrowest Obscura flow that matches the request:
21:    - `fetch` for one page or one extraction
22:    - `scrape` for multiple URLs in parallel
23:    - `serve` for Playwright or Puppeteer CDP connections
24: 5. Return one minimal command or one minimal code sample first.
25: 6. Add only the flags that matter for the user's goal such as `--stealth`, `--timeout`, `--wait-until`, `--output`, `--concurrency`, or `--quiet`.
26: 
27: ## Quick Start
28: 
29: Run `scripts/detect_obscura.py` first. It checks:
30: 
31: - whether `obscura` is on `PATH`
32: - whether `obscura-worker` is present in the same directory
33: - likely local binary locations on Windows, macOS, and Linux
34: 
35: If the binary is missing:

37: - Recommend the GitHub Releases archive for the user's platform.
38: - On Windows, remind the user to keep `obscura.exe` and `obscura-worker.exe` in the same folder for parallel `scrape`.
39: - If the user wants to build from source, mention `cargo build --release` and `cargo build --release --features stealth`.
40: 
41: ## Task Patterns
42: 
43: ### Local development with Vite
44: 
45: Treat this as the default answer when users want Obscura to hit `http://localhost:5173` or another local Vite port.
46: 
47: Recommended flow:
48: 
49: 1. Keep Vite running locally.
50: 2. Expose the Vite port with `hostc`.
51: 3. Give Obscura the resulting public `https://` URL.
52: 
53: Use `scripts/command_templates.py vite-hostc` to generate the shortest working command set.
54: Use `scripts/command_templates.py vite-hostc-cdp` when the user wants the hostc flow plus a ready-to-run Playwright or Puppeteer snippet.
55: 
56: Minimal sequence:
57: 
58: ```powershell
59: pnpm dev
60: npx hostc 5173
61: obscura fetch https://your-hostc-url --dump html
62: ```
63: 
64: If the user needs browser automation instead of one fetch:
65: 
66: ```powershell
67: obscura serve --port 9222
68: ```

70: Then provide a Playwright or Puppeteer snippet that navigates to the hostc URL.
71: 
72: Example:

75: python scripts/command_templates.py vite-hostc-cdp playwright --public-url https://your-hostc-url
76: ```
77: 
78: ### Local development with listhen
79: 
80: Use this only as a backup option when the user explicitly wants `listhen` or already has it. The important part is the public tunnel URL, not the local listener.
81: 
82: Do not recommend:

84: - `localhost`
85: - `127.0.0.1`
86: - LAN IPs such as `192.168.x.x`

89: ### Single-page extraction

91: Use `scripts/command_templates.py fetch` to build a starter command, then adapt it.
92: 
93: Common examples:
94: 
95: ```powershell
96: obscura fetch https://example.com --eval "document.title"
97: obscura fetch https://example.com --dump links
98: obscura fetch https://news.ycombinator.com --dump html --wait-until networkidle0
99: ```
100: 
101: Prefer:
102: 
103: - `--eval` for one DOM expression or computed value
104: - `--dump html|text|links` for built-in output modes
105: - `--output` when the user wants a file

107: ### Parallel scraping

114: obscura scrape https://example.com https://example.org --concurrency 10 --eval "document.querySelector('h1')?.textContent" --format json
115: ```

117: Prefer `--quiet` when the output is meant for scripts or piping.

119: ### CDP server for Playwright or Puppeteer

122:

1: # Treads 🌿
2: 
3: > *Step outside. Notice what lives.*
4: 
5: Treads is a mindful, local-first naturalist companion that turns outdoor walks into observational field journals. It combines pedestrian loop generation, on-device AI species identification, Wikipedia-verified naturalist notes, voice observation capture, tactile sensory cues, and one-tap Obsidian vault exports.
6: 
7: Built for the **Google AI Studio / Gemini Naturalist Challenge**.

9: ---

11: ## Key Highlights
12: 
13: - **🔒 100% Local-First & Privacy Sovereign (`CONS-01` - `CONS-04`):**
14:   - All field observations, GPS breadcrumbs, photos, and voice notes live directly in browser IndexedDB.
15:   - EXIF GPS metadata is stripped before client queries.
16:   - Strict first-visit privacy consent gate with durable storage request (`navigator.storage.persist()`).
17: 
18: - **🧭 Pedestrian Loop Navigation (`WALK-01` - `WALK-03`):**
19:   - Interactive MapLibre GL vector maps with outdoor topography tiles.
20:   - Suggested walking loops (15m, 30m, 45m) generated via OpenRouteService pedestrian routing.
21:   - Background-resilient GPS tracking with 35m accuracy filtering and automatic wake resumption.
22: 
23: - **🔍 Two-Tap Taxonomic Species Identification (`CAPT-01`, `EVAL-01`):**
24:   - Multimodal vision identification powered by Google Gemini.
25:   - Returns up to 3 candidate species with taxonomic ranks and confidence scoring.
26:   - Honest refusal engine refusing non-living inanimate objects and human portraits.
27:   - Headless 30-fixture evaluation suite (`pnpm test:eval`) verifying ≥70% organism accuracy and ≥90% honest refusal rate.
28: 
29: - **📖 Wikipedia Educational Fact Cards (`SPEC-01`):**
30:   - Three verified sentence-level natural history facts linked to source Wikipedia citations.
31:   - Cached for offline retrieval.
32: 
33: - **🖋️ Tegaki Handwriting & Cuelume Sensory Polish (`DSGN-03` - `DSGN-05`):**
34:   - Progressive Japanese Tegaki-style ink handwriting reveal with `Caveat` font and `prefers-reduced-motion` bypass.
35:   - Dual-oscillator synthesized Web Audio chimes (E5–G#5 major third capture chime, C5–E5–G5–C6 celebration arpeggio).
36:   - Tactile native haptic vibration (`navigator.vibrate`) on capture and hunt victory.
37: 
38: - **🎙️ Voice Observation Notes & Speech (`VOIC-01`, `VOIC-02`):**
39:   - Voice recording with live canvas waveform visualization.
40:   - ElevenLabs speech-to-text transcription and high-fidelity text-to-speech naturalist narration.

42: - **🎯 Daily Species Hunt Challenge (`HUNT-01`, `HUNT-02`):**

# Treads 🌿 — Hacktoberfest Touch Grass

> *Step outside. Notice what lives.*

Treads is a mindful, local-first naturalist companion designed to get you outside and observing nature. Built for **Hacktoberfest Touch Grass**, it turns outdoor walks into rich observational field journals using open-weight AI (**Gemma 4**), tactile audio-haptic cues, high-fidelity voice journaling via **ElevenLabs**, MapLibre pedestrian loops, and one-tap Obsidian vault exports.

---

## 🍃 Core Philosophy: Mindful, Grounded, and Local-First

Unlike social-feed nature apps that harvest location traces or gatekeep data behind cloud logins, Treads operates on four core principles:
1. **100% Local-First Data Sovereignty:** Your field journal, specimen photographs, voice notes, and GPS routes live solely in browser IndexedDB (Dexie). No accounts, no trackers, and no remote databases.
2. **Client-Side EXIF Stripping:** Photos are decoded directly onto an HTML5 Canvas, stripping 100% of EXIF hardware and GPS location metadata client-side before any AI inference.
3. **Open-Weight AI via Gemma 4:** Naturalist intelligence powered by open-weight **Gemma 4** (`gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`) for species identification, factual natural history grounding, sensory observation prompts, and Aldo Leopold-style walk dispatches.
4. **Honest Taxon Verification & Refusal:** Treads refuses inanimate objects and human portraits with educational explanations, bounds AI species proposals against the live Wikipedia Action API, and scrubs toxicity or foraging claims automatically.

---

## 🧠 Gemma 4 & ElevenLabs Integration

### 1. Gemma 4 Open-Weight AI Architecture (`gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`)
Treads integrates Google's open-weight Gemma 4 model across the field journey:
- **Two-Tap Taxonomic Identification (`/api/identify`):**
  - Evaluates photographs alongside regional context (coarse latitude/longitude to 1 decimal place) and observation month for phenological accuracy.
  - Generates up to 3 candidate species ordered by likelihood with confidence tiers (`Likely`, `Possible`, `Unsure`) and taxonomic kinds (`tree`, `flower`, `plant`, `bird`, `insect`, `fungus`, `animal`).
  - Cross-references each proposed binomial against the Wikipedia Action API to eliminate hallucinations.
  - Implements an **Honest Refusal Engine**: strictly rejects cups, bicycles, benches, asphalt, and human portraits with thoughtful naturalist guidance rather than hallucinating classifications.
- **Wikipedia-Grounded Natural History Synthesis (`/api/facts`):**
  - Fetches the lead section of Wikipedia for confirmed taxa, segmented into numbered sentences.
  - Instructs Gemma 4 to distill a 40-word summary and up to 3 sentence-level biological facts citing specific source sentence indices.
  - Enforces a strict negative constraint with an automated safety scrubber: drops edibility, foraging, and medicinal claims to prevent dangerous consumption.
  - **"Look Closely" Sensory Observation Prompts:** Generates a real-time observation prompt directing the walker to look closely at a physical tactile feature right in front of them (e.g. leaf veins, bark ridges, petal margins, pollen sacs, wing borders).
- **Aldo Leopold Field Dispatches & Ecological Web (`/api/walk/dispatch`):**
  - When completing a walk, Gemma 4 synthesizes the session's observed species, voice notes, duration, and terrain into a poetic 2-3 sentence field dispatch reminiscent of classic naturalist prose.
  - Identifies ecological interconnections (food sources, host plants, pollination, mycorrhizal networks) between species encountered on the same walk to map an **Observed Ecological Web**.

### 2. ElevenLabs Voice & Speech Engine
- **Field Voice Journaling (`/api/transcribe`):**
  - Hands-free field recording engine with real-time Web Audio `AnalyserNode` live waveform visualization, 60-second circular timer limit, and slide-to-cancel gestures.
  - Transcribes voice notes using **ElevenLabs Scribe STT** (`scribe_v1`) with automatic language detection and word-level timestamps.
  - Graceful Web Speech API and offline mock fallback when offline or without an API key.
- **Naturalist Speech Narration (`/api/speak`):**
  - Natural history fact cards feature a one-tap "Listen" narration button.
  - Streams high-fidelity natural narration via **ElevenLabs Multilingual v2** (`eleven_multilingual_v2`) using the calm, warm nature voice *Rachel* (`21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM`).
  - Seamless fallback to browser `window.speechSynthesis` when running in offline or demo modes.

---

## 🗺️ Application Routes & Feature Tour

### User Routes
- **`/` — The Field Hearth (Dashboard):**
  - Active walk launcher with duration goal picker (15m, 30m, 45m).
  - Daily Species Hunt challenge with rotating targets across birds, trees, insects, and fungi.
  - Recent field notes preview and total lifetime naturalist statistics.
  - Tegaki ink handwriting cards and warm bone-paper aesthetic.
- **`/walk` — Active Field Exploration:**
  - Full-screen MapLibre GL outdoor topography vector map powered by OpenFreeMap.
  - Pedestrian round-trip loop generation via OpenRouteService (`/api/route`).
  - Background-resilient GPS tracking with 35m accuracy filtering and live terracotta trail polyline.
  - Camera shutter dock with instant canvas EXIF stripping and bottom-sheet identification flow.
  - Audio recorder bottom sheet with live waveform visualization and slide-to-cancel.
  - Hold-to-finish 1.5s confirmation press preventing accidental termination in pockets.
  - Post-walk celebration drawer with Aldo Leopold field dispatch and ecological connections.
- **`/collection` — Herbarium & Life List:**
  - Visual grid of all cataloged flora, fauna, and fungi categorized by taxonomic kingdom.
  - Filter by group (`All`, `Trees`, `Flowers`, `Birds`, `Insects`, `Fungi`, `Animals`).
  - Search bar with instant local indexing over common and binomial scientific names.
  - Completion badges for daily hunt targets.
- **`/journal` — Field Logbook:**
  - Chronological timeline of completed walking expeditions.
  - Walk distance, duration, elevation, trail map miniatures, and specimen thumbnails.
  - One-tap **Obsidian-Compatible Vault Export** (`EXP-01`): downloads a zipped archive containing structured Markdown notes with YAML frontmatter, organized specimen photos, and a complete JSON database backup.
- **`/journal/[walkId]` — Walk Expedition Detail:**
  - Interactive map replaying the exact GPS path, observation markers, and breadcrumbs.
  - Complete list of finds with photo cards, notes, voice recordings, and ecological web.
- **`/entry/[id]` — Specimen Observation Note:**
  - High-resolution photo viewer with capture metadata (timestamp, coarse location, confidence).
  - Grounded natural history fact card with source Wikipedia citations.
  - One-tap audio narration playback powered by ElevenLabs.
  - "Look Closely" sensory prompt and candidate species re-identification interface.
- **`/settings` — Preferences & Sovereignty:**
  - Audio chimes toggle (Cuelume dual-oscillator synthesizer: E5–G#5 capture chime, C5–E5–G5–C6 celebration arpeggio).
  - Haptic feedback toggle (`navigator.vibrate`).
  - Storage persistence manager (`navigator.storage.persist()`).
  - Full data backup export and local database reset controls.
- **`/privacy` — Transparent Data Manifesto:**
  - Granular breakdown of what stays on device (100% of notes, photos, and GPS routes) versus transient API queries (EXIF-stripped images, coarse coordinates, audio blobs).

### Developer & Benchmark Routes
- **`/eval` — Interactive Taxonomic Evaluation Harness:**
  - Visual 30-specimen benchmark dashboard evaluating 20 living organisms and 10 negative refusal cases.
  - Live accuracy score, refusal rate gauge, latency metrics, and candidate inspection.
- **`/spike` — Hardware & API Verification Suite:**
  - Live diagnostic panel testing MapLibre GL rendering, GPS sensor precision, Web Audio synthesizer chimes, camera capture canvas pipelines, ElevenLabs speech synthesis, and Gemma 4 structured generation.

---

## 📊 Evaluation & Verification Benchmark

Treads includes a headless 30-fixture evaluation harness (`scripts/run-eval-suite.ts`) validating organism classification and honest refusal:
- **Living Organism Fixtures:** 20 test specimens spanning trees, wildflowers, birds, insects, and fungi.
- **Negative Refusal Fixtures:** 10 non-organism and human subjects (bicycles, coffee mugs, asphalt, park benches, water bottles, human portraits, outdoor selfies).

### Benchmark Criteria & Live Gemma 4 Results:
| Metric | Benchmark Target | Live Gemma 4 (`gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`) | Deterministic Mock Engine |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Organism Accuracy** | ≥ 70.0% | **95.0%** (19 / 20) | **100.0%** (20 / 20) |
| **Honest Refusal Rate** | ≥ 90.0% | **100.0%** (10 / 10) | **100.0%** (10 / 10) |
| **Average Latency** | — | **~2,086 ms** | **~14 ms** |

Run the headless benchmark locally:
```bash
# Offline deterministic benchmark
pnpm test:eval

# Live benchmark with Gemma 4 (requires GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY in .env.local)
pnpm tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/run-eval-suite.ts
```

> **Note on Fixtures:** The 30 evaluation fixtures in `public/eval-fixtures/` use stylized SVG illustrations for deterministic, portable, offline-capable verification across test runners without multi-megabyte binary dependencies.

---

## 🛠️ Tech Stack

- **Framework:** Next.js 16.4 (App Router, Turbopack) & React 19
- **Open-Weight AI:** Google Gemma 4 (`gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`) via `@ai-sdk/google` & Vercel `ai` SDK
- **Voice & Speech:** ElevenLabs Scribe STT (`scribe_v1`) & ElevenLabs Multilingual TTS (`eleven_multilingual_v2`)
- **UI & Tokens:** Tailwind CSS v4, Base UI primitives, Lucide React, Japanese Tegaki ink styling (`Caveat` font), and Hairline isometric line figures
- **Database:** Dexie 4.4 (IndexedDB) with `dexie-react-hooks`
- **Mapping & Routing:** MapLibre GL 6.13 with OpenFreeMap vector tiles and OpenRouteService pedestrian routing
- **Sensory Audio & Motion:** Web Audio API (Cuelume dual-oscillator synthesizer) & Motion (Framer Motion)
- **Data Export:** JSZip for Obsidian Markdown + YAML vault bundling

---

## 🚀 Getting Started

### 1. Install Dependencies
```bash
pnpm install
```

### 2. Configure Environment Variables
Create a `.env.local` file with your API keys (see `.env.example`):
```bash
# Google AI Studio (Open-Weight Gemma 4)
GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY=your_gemini_or_gemma_api_key
IDENTIFY_MODEL_ID=gemma-4-26b-a4b-it
FACTS_MODEL_ID=gemma-4-26b-a4b-it

# ElevenLabs (Voice transcription & high-fidelity narration)
ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=your_elevenlabs_api_key

# OpenRouteService (Pedestrian loop round trips)
ORS_API_KEY=your_ors_api_key

# Optional: Upstash Redis (Server rate-limiting; uses in-memory in development)
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL=
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN=
```

### 3. Run Development Server
```bash
pnpm dev
```
Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) in your browser.

### 4. Run the Evaluation Suite

# Treads 🌿 — Hacktoberfest Touch Grass

> *Step outside. Notice what lives.*

Treads is a mindful, local-first naturalist companion designed to encourage outdoor observation and mindful walking. Built for **Hacktoberfest Touch Grass**, it turns routine neighborhood walks into observational field journals by weaving together on-device sensory experiences, pedestrian loop generation, open-weight machine intelligence, voice-recorded reflections, and seamless Obsidian vault exports.

---

## 🍃 Core Philosophy: Mindful, Grounded, and Local-First

Unlike conventional nature apps that require accounts, monetize social streams, and store location histories on remote servers, Treads is built around quiet craftsmanship and personal sovereignty:

- **100% Local-First Data Sovereignty:** Your field journal entries, specimen photographs, voice recordings, and GPS coordinates live entirely in your browser's IndexedDB (Dexie). No accounts, zero analytics trackers, and zero server-side persistence.
- **Client-Side Privacy & EXIF Stripping:** Captured specimens are rasterized directly onto an HTML5 Canvas to strip 100% of hardware and GPS metadata before any transient AI queries.
- **Open-Weight Intelligence via Gemma 4:** Powered by Google's open-weight **Gemma 4** (`gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`) across all intelligence layers—from phenology-aware taxonomic candidate ranking to grounded natural history synthesis and Aldo Leopold-style field dispatches.
- **Sensory Voice Journaling via ElevenLabs:** Hands-free field recordings are transcribed with word-level precision using **ElevenLabs Scribe STT** (`scribe_v1`), while natural history notes can be read aloud in the field via warm, studio-grade narration powered by **ElevenLabs Multilingual v2** (`eleven_multilingual_v2`).
- **Tactile Sensory Cues:** Synthesized Web Audio dual-oscillator chimes (E5–G#5 major-third capture chime, C5–E5–G5–C6 celebration arpeggio), Japanese Tegaki ink handwriting reveals (`Caveat`), and native haptic pulses ground digital interactions into calming outdoor rituals.

---

## 🗺️ Application Overview & Features

Treads organizes the naturalist experience across a focused set of views:

- **The Field Hearth (`/`):** Launch walks by selecting a loop duration goal (15m, 30m, 45m), view your active streak and field statistics, and discover the rotating **Daily Species Hunt** challenge across birds, trees, wildflowers, and fungi.
- **Active Field Walk (`/walk`):** Full-screen MapLibre GL outdoor topography maps with OpenRouteService pedestrian loops, background-resilient GPS trail tracking with 35m accuracy filtering, two-tap camera capture with instant canvas EXIF stripping, live-waveform voice recorder drawer, and a pocket-safe hold-to-finish confirmation dock.
- **Herbarium & Life List (`/collection`):** A visual catalog of all flora, fauna, and fungi documented on your walks, filterable by taxonomic kingdom with instant local search across common and binomial names.
- **Field Logbook (`/journal` & `/journal/[walkId]`):** Review past expeditions with route trail replays, elevation metrics, specimen finds, and one-tap **Obsidian-Compatible Vault Export** (producing a zipped archive of Markdown notes with YAML frontmatter, photos, and JSON backups).
- **Specimen Note (`/entry/[id]`):** High-resolution photo inspection, candidate species re-identification, grounded Wikipedia natural history cards with citations, tactile *"Look Closely"* sensory observation prompts, and studio-grade ElevenLabs voice narration.
- **Preferences & Sovereignty (`/settings` & `/privacy`):** Control audio chimes, native haptics, and durable browser storage persistence, or review the transparent data manifesto explaining our zero-server data model.
- **Developer & Benchmark Tools (`/eval` & `/spike`):** Interactive 30-fixture batch taxonomic evaluation dashboard and live hardware diagnostic suite for sensors, audio, and AI pipelines.

---

## 📊 Evaluation & Verification Benchmark

Treads includes a headless 30-fixture evaluation harness (`scripts/run-eval-suite.ts`) validating organism classification and honest refusal:
- **Living Organism Fixtures:** 20 test specimens spanning trees, wildflowers, birds, insects, and fungi.
- **Negative Refusal Fixtures:** 10 non-organism and human subjects (bicycles, coffee mugs, asphalt, park benches, water bottles, human portraits, outdoor selfies).

### Benchmark Criteria & Live Gemma 4 Results:
| Metric | Benchmark Target | Live Gemma 4 (`gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`) | Deterministic Mock Engine |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Organism Accuracy** | ≥ 70.0% | **95.0%** (19 / 20) | **100.0%** (20 / 20) |
| **Honest Refusal Rate** | ≥ 90.0% | **100.0%** (10 / 10) | **100.0%** (10 / 10) |
| **Average Latency** | — | **~2,086 ms** | **~14 ms** |

Run the headless benchmark locally:
```bash
# Offline deterministic benchmark
pnpm test:eval

# Live benchmark with Gemma 4 (requires GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY in .env.local)
pnpm tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/run-eval-suite.ts
```

> **Note on Fixtures:** The 30 evaluation fixtures in `public/eval-fixtures/` use stylized SVG illustrations for deterministic, portable, offline-capable verification across test runners without multi-megabyte binary dependencies.

---

## 🛠️ Tech Stack

- **Framework:** Next.js 16.4 (App Router, Turbopack) & React 19
- **Open-Weight AI:** Google Gemma 4 (`gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`) via `@ai-sdk/google` & Vercel `ai` SDK
- **Voice & Speech:** ElevenLabs Scribe STT (`scribe_v1`) & ElevenLabs Multilingual TTS (`eleven_multilingual_v2`)
- **UI & Tokens:** Tailwind CSS v4, Base UI primitives, Lucide React, Japanese Tegaki ink styling (`Caveat` font), and Hairline isometric line figures
- **Database:** Dexie 4.4 (IndexedDB) with `dexie-react-hooks`
- **Mapping & Routing:** MapLibre GL 6.13 with OpenFreeMap vector tiles and OpenRouteService pedestrian routing
- **Sensory Audio & Motion:** Web Audio API (Cuelume dual-oscillator synthesizer) & Motion (Framer Motion)
- **Data Export:** JSZip for Obsidian Markdown + YAML vault bundling

---

## 🚀 Getting Started

### 1. Install Dependencies
```bash
pnpm install
```

### 2. Configure Environment Variables
Create a `.env.local` file with your API keys (see `.env.example`):
```bash
# Google AI Studio (Open-Weight Gemma 4)
GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY=your_gemini_or_gemma_api_key
IDENTIFY_MODEL_ID=gemma-4-26b-a4b-it
FACTS_MODEL_ID=gemma-4-26b-a4b-it

# ElevenLabs (Voice transcription & high-fidelity narration)
ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=your_elevenlabs_api_key

# OpenRouteService (Pedestrian loop round trips)
ORS_API_KEY=your_ors_api_key

# Optional: Upstash Redis (Server rate-limiting; uses in-memory in development)
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL=
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN=
```

### 3. Run Development Server
```bash
pnpm dev
```
Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) in your browser.

### 4. Run the Evaluation Suite
```bash
pnpm test:eval
```

### 5. Production Build
```bash
pnpm build
```

---

## 🌿 Field Verification Protocol

For the complete 8-step outdoor field walkthrough protocol covering GPS tracking, photo capture, EXIF stripping, voice transcription, and Obsidian export, refer to [`FIELD-VERIFICATION.md`](./FIELD-VERIFICATION.md).

args.CodeContent:
# Treads 🌿

> Step outside. Notice what lives.

Treads is a mindful, local-first naturalist companion and field journal built for Hacktoberfest Touch Grass. It guides outdoor walkers with pedestrian loop generation, identifies living flora, fauna, and fungi using open-weight AI (Google Gemma 4), captures voice reflections via ElevenLabs, grounds natural history notes in Wikipedia, and exports observational field journals into Obsidian vaults.

## Core Pillars
- Local-First Privacy: 100% of user field journals, specimen photos, GPS breadcrumbs, and voice notes live strictly in browser IndexedDB (Dexie). No accounts or tracking databases.
- Client-Side EXIF Stripping: Captured photos are rasterized on an HTML5 Canvas to remove 100% of EXIF and GPS hardware metadata before transient AI analysis.
- Open-Weight AI (Gemma 4): Uses `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` via `@ai-sdk/google` for phenology-aware taxonomic ranking, Wikipedia-grounded natural history synthesis, tactile "Look Closely" sensory prompts, and Aldo Leopold-style field dispatches.
- ElevenLabs Audio & Speech: High-fidelity field journaling via ElevenLabs Scribe STT (`scribe_v1`) and natural speech narration via ElevenLabs Multilingual v2 (`eleven_multilingual_v2`, voice: Rachel).
- Tactile & Sensory Feedback: Dual-oscillator Web Audio synthesized chimes (E5–G#5 major third, C5–E5–G5–C6 celebration arpeggio), Japanese Tegaki ink handwriting reveals (`Caveat`), and native haptic vibration.
- Obsidian Vault Export: One-tap export generating a zip archive with YAML-frontmatter Markdown notes, organized photographs, and full JSON database backups.

## Key Routes & Architecture
- `/`: The Field Hearth — active walk launcher with 15m/30m/45m loop goals, daily species hunt targets, and naturalist lifetime stats.
- `/walk`: Active Field Walk — full-screen MapLibre GL outdoor topography maps, OpenRouteService pedestrian loops, 35m accuracy-filtered GPS tracking, canvas EXIF stripping camera dock, live-waveform voice recorder, and pocket-safe hold-to-confirm finish.
- `/collection`: Herbarium & Life List — visual catalog of observed species categorized by kingdom with instant local text search.
- `/journal`: Field Logbook — chronological walk expeditions with GPS replays, elevation metrics, species counts, and Obsidian export.
- `/journal/[walkId]`: Walk Expedition Detail — interactive GPS trail replay and species encounter breakdown.
- `/entry/[id]`: Specimen Observation Note — high-resolution photo inspector, Wikipedia natural history fact cards, ElevenLabs audio narration, sensory observation prompt, and re-identification.
- `/settings`: Audio chimes, native haptics, and durable browser storage persistence.
- `/privacy`: Transparent data manifesto detailing local-first zero-server privacy architecture.
- `/eval`: Interactive 30-specimen benchmark harness scoring taxonomic accuracy (≥70%) and honest refusal (≥90%).
- `/spike`: Hardware & API diagnostic panel testing maps, GPS sensors, audio synthesizers, camera canvas, and AI endpoints.

## Technical Specifications
- Framework: Next.js 16.4 (App Router, Turbopack) & React 19
- Styling & Components: Tailwind CSS v4, Base UI primitives, Lucide React, Caveat, Fraunces, Hanken Grotesk, JetBrains Mono
- Database: Dexie 4.4 (IndexedDB) with dexie-react-hooks
- Maps: MapLibre GL 6.13 with OpenFreeMap vector tiles
- AI & Speech: Google Gemma 4 (`gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`), ElevenLabs Scribe & Multilingual v2
- Repository: https://github.com/Zephyrxx0/treads

   - Implemented standard Next.js App Router dynamic route handler generating `/robots.txt`.

   - Disallows `/api/`, `/eval`, and `/spike`.

3. **Added `llms.txt` (`public/llms.txt`):**
   - Formatted structured context for LLM crawlers outlining Treads' architecture, open-weight Gemma 4 and ElevenLabs integrations, local-first IndexedDB privacy model, all application routes, and tech stack details.
